answer: Spectral Wait Curve: each new identity starts at a low trust score and can only rise along a curve set by verified age and activity; rewards scale with score while costs (fees, exposure limits) stay flat. Cloning yields identities stuck on the curve's flat dune, earning little. Genuine agents climb past a ridge where rewards outpace duplication cost, so an attacker must fund each clone through the full wait. A rare opal-tier score is reachable only after sustained paid activity, making bulk fabrication cost the sum of all those waits.
